pearls: Acts only at **γ-containing** GABA-A receptors (α1, α2, α3, α5); **δ-containing extrasynaptic** (tonic) receptors are benzodiazepine-insensitive
Subtype roles: α1 = **daytime sedation**, amnesia, anticonvulsant action; α2/α3 = **muscle relaxant** and alcohol-potentiating effects; α5 (hippocampus) = cognition
Part of the **mesolimbic reward** system's drugs of abuse; alcoholics often also abuse benzodiazepines, so screen for substance use before prescribing
**Not recommended** for agitation in dementia; sedatives (including benzodiazepines) raise **aspiration** and pneumonia risk
Can be a **second-line sleep aid** in fibromyalgia, and an add-on to an SSRI in OCD
uses: Also sleep induction, anticonvulsant and muscle relaxant actions (Chapter 3)
**GAD and panic disorder** (benzodiazepine class use, Chapter 8)

sideEffects.e: **Sedation and unsteady gait** (reported with second-line agents for dementia agitation; the book also calls α2δ ligands not particularly sedating for sleep)

pearls: **Open-channel, use-dependent** binding: blocks the most active N and P/Q channels and leaves closed channels, so normal transmission is spared
Pain may be best treated **early**: blocking central sensitization could stop pain being imprinted and progressing to chronic states
In fibromyalgia, combine with an **SNRI** for additive pain relief and broader coverage (α2δ: anxiety, slow-wave sleep; SNRI: depression, fatigue, fibro-fog)
If response is inadequate, **sodium-channel anticonvulsants** (second-line for neuropathic pain) act differently and may still work
Listed as a possible **second-line** option for agitation in dementia (not valproate, topiramate, oxcarbazepine or benzodiazepines)

pearls: **Naloxone** reverses acute morphine effects but precipitates withdrawal in dependent patients
Short-half-life agonists give **intense, brief** withdrawal; methadone is milder but longer (peak 72-96 h, 14+ days)
**Fentanyl** is about 100 times, and carfentanil about 10,000 times, as potent as morphine
**Spares normal sensory input**: Aβ fibers lack μ receptors
Opioid analgesics lose effect with long-term use and are **limited in amount and duration**
